body:
AppVeyor build [9193](https://ci.appveyor.com/project/nlohmann/json/builds/54896795) on `develop` fails since #5634 (Zmij double writer):

- **VS2015 (all three jobs):** `zmij.hpp(187): warning C4554: '<<': check operator precedence` — a false positive on `(p.high << static_cast<unsigned>(64 - extra_shift)) | (p.low >> static_cast<unsigned>(extra_shift))` despite the parentheses; with `/W4 /WX` nothing builds. The shift amounts are now named `constexpr unsigned` constants, so the expression has no casts.
- **VS2017, C++17 shard 1/2 (x86 and x64):** `test-to_chars_cpp17` fails 16 checks at `unit-to_chars.cpp:713`, all for two-digit outputs (`0.25`, `16.0`, `1.6e-322`, …). The test built the one-digit-shorter candidates with `std::scientific << std::setprecision(digits.size() - 2)`; MSVC 2017's library ignores a precision of 0, so the "shorter" candidate was the value itself. The test now truncates the digits instead: the value lies within half a unit of the last printed digit, so the truncated digits and their successor are the closest shorter candidates (the existing `mid - 1, mid, mid + 1` loop keeps covering them). The now unused `<iomanip>`, `<sstream>`, `<locale>` includes are dropped.

Checked locally with clang (C++11 and C++17, `-Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Werror`): the to_chars test passes with the same 623,597 assertions. Neither MSVC version is available locally, so AppVeyor confirms the fix.

## Public API

No breaking changes: the library change only renames internal shift amounts in `detail::zmij`; output is unchanged.
